page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.7xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon 8163 processors running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is consistently weak, as evidenced by bottom 25% scores in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression, alongside a poor bottom 10% rating in single-threaded gzip compression. However, the 32 dedicated cores compensate in parallelized tasks, achieving average middle 50% ratings in multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth tests also fall into the average tier for both small and large block reads and writes, though the Passmark memory score is weak.

Given the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-core capabilities, this instance is suited for workloads that scale across multiple threads rather than relying on high single-thread velocity. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and Redis caching, all of which achieved average performance tiers in testing. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation provides predictable multi-threaded execution, but the lower single-core efficiency suggests it is less optimal for single-threaded serialization or latency-sensitive sequential processing.
